children: rebounded 4.85% to $213.82 in premarket trading at 8:59 a.m. ET on November 18 as early reviews of Grand Theft Auto VI landed a 99/100 Metacritic score. Shares had fallen 4.47% to $203.93 on November 17, the day before the game's global rollout began.

Investing.com cited Sensor Tower data showing 15.88 million preorder units, and Oppenheimer estimates of about 20 million units and more than $1.85 billion of gross revenue in the first three days. Take-Two's own fiscal second-quarter release confirmed the November 19 launch on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, reported net bookings down 18% to $1.60 billion, and reiterated fiscal 2027 net bookings guidance of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion, including $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion for the December quarter.

If the three-day estimate holds, GTA VI alone would deliver more than half of the December-quarter bookings guide, though gross revenue is not the same as net bookings after platform fees. GuruFocus gives Take-Two a GF Score of 75/100, with mid-range profitability and balance sheet ranks and weak momentum. Its GF Value of $221.08 sits about 3% above the premarket price, so GuruFocus sees the shares as fairly valued and the launch largely expected. The next test is the first official sales disclosure, which Oppenheimer said could come as early as November 20.

title: Take-Two Stocks Rise 4.85% Premarket as GTA VI Hits 99 Metacritic Before Launch
